notes: Tests definitional what a bare tu label tells us. Corrected after the Wave 1 agent source review: questions and rubrics distinguish procedure scope, supported alternatives and missing deployment inputs. Claims: tby-turbidity-unit-generic-01, tby-jtu-ftu-obsolete-01, a60-tbl601-units-01, tby-nephelometry-definition-01, tby-fnu-family-wavelength-01, tby-ntu-family-wavelength-01, tby-t4-ntu-fnu-90deg-01, tby-t6-fnmu-fnu-expansion-01. turns.content: We inherited a folder of old clarity readings and the column is just headed 'TU'. What does a bare label like that actually tell us about those numbers?

must_contain: states that TU stands for turbidity units
states that it is a generic label, used for turbidity measured on instruments whose design is not specified
states that because the instrument design is unknown, the label does not tell you what light source or optical arrangement produced the number
warns that older data can also carry historical labels - Jackson turbidity units (JTU) or formazin turbidity units (FTU) - which are no longer in normal use
must_not: treats TU as equivalent to NTU or to FNU
invents a conversion factor between TU and any modern turbidity unit
assumes the old readings came from a particular manufacturer or instrument

turns.content: So for our own gear, what decides which of those labels we're supposed to write on the readings? Is it just a house style we pick once?

must_contain: states that the label is not a matter of preference - it is determined by the instrument's optical design
States broad-spectrum 400-680 nm light corresponds to NTU, NTRU, BU, AU and NTMU, while FNU, FNRU, FBU, FAU and FNMU generally correspond to 780-900 nm near-infrared light.

states that the detector arrangement sets the other half: a detector at 90 degrees to the beam is nephelometry and gives the plain nephelometric labels, while backscatter, attenuation, ratio and multibeam arrangements each have their own distinct labels
gives what the letters expand to for at least the two common cases - NTU as nephelometric turbidity units and FNU as formazin nephelometric units
must_not: says the unit can be chosen freely as long as the fleet is consistent
invents a parameter code or a wavelength figure not supported by the source
answers from the operator range table's NTU baselines instead of the naming rule
